statement: A rectangle is cut into four smaller rectangles by one line parallel to its length and one line parallel to its width. The top-left small rectangle has area $12$, the top-right one has area $18$, and the bottom-left one has area $30$. What is the area of the original rectangle?

choices.misconception: I added the three given areas, 12 + 18 + 30 = 60, and forgot the fourth small rectangle.
I thought the bottom-right rectangle has the same area as the top-right one, 18, because they are in the same column, and got 60 + 18 = 78. They have the same width but not the same height.
I set up the ratio upside down: I said the bottom-right area is to 30 as 12 is to 18, so it came out 20 and the total was 80.
I thought the areas go up by the same amount across a row: the top row goes up by 6, so I made the bottom-right 30 + 6 = 36 and got 96.

hints: Two rectangles in the same row have the same height, so the ratio of their areas is the ratio of their widths.
The top row shows that the right column is $\frac{18}{12} = \frac{3}{2}$ times as wide as the left column. That is true in the bottom row too.
The bottom-right rectangle has area $30 \cdot \frac{3}{2} = 45$. Add all four areas.

solutions.reliable: The two top rectangles have the same height, so their widths are in the ratio $12 : 18 = 2 : 3$. The two bottom rectangles have those same two widths and share a height, so their areas are also in the ratio $2 : 3$. The bottom-left area is $30$, so the bottom-right area is $30 \cdot \frac{3}{2} = 45$. The original rectangle has area $12 + 18 + 30 + 45 = 105$.
solutions.elegant: The top row has area $12 + 18 = 30$ and the left column has area $12 + 30 = 42$. Multiplying them gives (width of the whole) $\times$ (top height) $\times$ (left width) $\times$ (height of the whole), and dividing by the top-left area, (left width) $\times$ (top height), leaves the whole area: $\frac{30 \cdot 42}{12} = 105$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
